item.title: Weil Weighs Wind-Down at GM Building, BXP Talks 7 Times Square Sale at $750M | NYC CRE News Oct 30, 2026
item.description:
It's Friday, October 30th. Welcome to the Anton Group News of the Day, I'm Eric Michael Anton. The ten-year Treasury closed Thursday at four point nine eight percent. Sofer is at 3.94. Weil Gotshal's leaders have recommended winding down the firm, with a partner vote expected in the coming days. Weil fills about 400,000 square feet at the GM Building, so a big block of trophy space on Fifth Avenue could come back to market. BXP posted third-quarter revenue of $911 million, up four point six percent. It's also negotiating to sell 7 Times Square for up to $750 million. Big REITs are selling Midtown towers to fund new development, and that keeps large office trades coming. BXP is also in talks with a tenant for five floors at 343 Madison. That would take the new tower to nearly 70 percent pre-leased, more proof that new trophy space still wins. One more. On this day in 1938, Orson Welles broadcast The War of the Worlds live from the Columbia Broadcasting Building at 485 Madison Avenue. It was staged as breaking news about Martians landing in New Jersey. An estimated six million people tuned in, and Welles was just twenty-three. That's New York. Have a great weekend.

Sources:

  • - U.S. Treasury, 10-year yield on 10/29/2026: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/daily-treasury-rates.csv/2026/all?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve
  • - New York Fed, SOFR on 10/28/2026: https://markets.newyorkfed.org/api/rates/secured/sofr/last/2.json

item.title: 71 Fifth Leasehold Trades for $62M, St. Brigid Site $35M, Fed Holds | NYC CRE News Oct 29, 2026
item.description:
It's Thursday, October 29th. Welcome to the Anton Group News of the Day, I'm Eric Michael Anton. The ten-year Treasury closed Wednesday at five point oh five percent. Sofer is at 3.95. The Fed held rates at three seventy-five to four percent yesterday. Two members voted for a hike, so keep that risk in your refinancing math. Namdar bought the leasehold at 71 Fifth Avenue in the Flatiron for $62 million. That's far below its 2021 pricing talk, and Manhattan office is still finding its true level. The Archdiocese is selling the former St. Brigid School site on Tompkins Square Park for $35 million. Quinlan plans an eleven-story rental there, as church land keeps feeding new housing. One more. Savanna and Deutsche Bank are pushing off the foreclosure sale of 521 Fifth Avenue again. A June appraisal valued the tower at $270 million, well below what Savanna paid. That's New York. See you tomorrow.

Sources:

  • - Treasury.gov daily par yield curve rates (10-yr, 10/28/2026)
  • - NY Fed SOFR (10/27/2026): https://markets.newyorkfed.org/api/rates/secured/sofr/last/3.json
  • - MarketWatch, Fed hold: https://www.marketwatch.com/story/u-s-stocks-up-treasury-yields-mixed-after-fed-hold-dbd6e218
  • - Commercial Observer, 71 Fifth Ave: https://commercialobserver.com/2026/10/71-fifth-avenue-leasehold-sale-namdar-realty-group/
  • - Patch, St. Brigid: https://patch.com/new-york/east-village/11-story-tower-could-rise-over-tompkins-square-park-after-35m-sale
  • - Commercial Observer, 521 Fifth Ave: https://commercialobserver.com/2026/10/savanna-deutsche-bank-521-fifth-avenue-foreclosure-sale/

item.title: October 26, 2026
item.description:
The 10-year Treasury fell to 5% last week with SOFR at 3.90%, as foreign capital returns to New York office through Tishman Speyer and Bouwinvest's Chrysler Building fund and 350 Park closes a $3.3 billion construction loan. Also: the Kips Bay AMC closes in January as NYU Langone expands, and the City Council passed COPA, giving nonprofits first shot at about 2,100 distressed rental buildings.

Sources:

  • U.S. Treasury daily par yield curve
  • New York Fed SOFR
  • Commercial Observer: Tishman Speyer and Bouwinvest U.S. office fund
  • GlobeNewswire: Vornado, Ken Griffin and Rudin close 350 Park joint venture, lease and construction loan
  • Variety: AMC Kips Bay closing date
  • The Real Deal: COPA passes NYC Council
